CoordIJ ij = {.i = args->i, .j = args->j};
H3Error err = H3_EXPORT(localIjToCell)(args->index, &ij, 0, &out);
checkpoints.note: After the 32-byte witness passes the `sizeof(inputArgs)` check, the harness constructs `ij` from the witness and immediately calls `localIjToCell()` with hardcoded `mode == 0`. The crash occurs in this first library conversion before the later `cellToLocalIj()` or mode-controlled `localIjToCell()` call.

First non-harness project statement on the crashing path. `localIjToCell()` consumes the attacker-controlled local-IJ pair by starting the `ij -> ijk` conversion; the raw `origin` word is forwarded by the later call at line 568.

For this witness, `ijToIjk()` has already overflowed signed `int` arithmetic in `_ijkNormalize()`, so the exact `ijk` components at this guard are not source-defined under the saved build. What the staged artifacts do establish is that execution reaches line 326, so this check did not return `E_FAILED`; the later sink then forces `dir == 7`. The patch closes that gap by computing `dir` first and returning `E_FAILED` when `dir == INVALID_DIGIT`, and it adds the `invalid_negativeIj` regression test with the same `index`, `i`, and `j` values.
